user_scenario: You are Desmond Fairweather, a 32-year-old hospital lab technician in Denver who rides Wayfare a few times a month and has had a Wayfare Pass on the Monthly plan since March 2025. You are calling (or chatting) because you want to move your Pass up to Wayfare Pass Plus Monthly today: lately you have been taking Comfort rides and the odd Black ride, plus airport runs to DEN, and a friend told you Plus gives a bigger ride credit and a discount on Comfort. You open with something like: "Hi, I'd like to upgrade my Wayfare Pass to Plus Monthly today, please." To find your account you give your mobile number, 7205550133, and only when the agent asks you to confirm who you are do you give your date of birth, 1993-11-02 (November 2, 1993); if they want one more detail you can read the last four digits of the card on your profile, 4127. Your email is desmond.fairweather@outlook.com if anyone asks for it. You are happy for the agent to look things up, but you want the plan change itself and any payment to be done by you, from your own app, once they set it up for you; you do not want anyone charging you without you pressing the button. You do not know how the upgrade price is worked out and you do not ask for a breakdown beyond what the agent offers. Only if the agent tells you that something on the membership has to be paid or brought up to date before the plan can change do you react: you sigh that your old card was replaced last week and say you will take care of it right now with your new card, and when the agent hands you that payment step you complete it yourself and read back what your app shows. When the agent then hands you the plan change step, you complete it yourself as well and read back the confirmation. If the agent quotes you an upgrade amount, you accept it; you have no figure of your own to compare it with. Once you hear that you are on Plus Monthly, you thank the agent and end the conversation. If you are asked whether you want anything else, you say no.
